subject: Customer escalation: surge in 5xx/429 + DNS latency — containment & temporary fallbacks
messages:
From: Rachel Lin <rachel@brightcart.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Spike in 5xx/429 across checkout region (us-west-2)

Hi Soojin / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sudden surge of 5xx and 429 responses from your API in our us-west-2 checkout region starting ~08:45 PDT. Latency for tokenized generation requests jumped from ~120ms p95 to multiple-second tail, and our client-side automatic retries are producing large request bursts. Impact: checkout timeouts and aborted payments for ~12% of active users in the last hour.

Attached are a small excerpt of request logs and a CSV of outstanding retry/backlog spikes.

Key ask: can Redwood route our requests away from the failing path or apply circuit-breaking/fallbacks? We need an immediate mitigation while you triage root cause.

Attachments: incident-snapshot-20260707.log (text), request-backlog-0707.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Rachel Lin
Head of Site Reliability — BrightCart
ops@brightcart.com
From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Lin <rachel@brightcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Spike in 5xx/429 across checkout region (us-west-2)

Rachel — thanks for the heads-up and the logs. We're treating as SEV-1.

Immediate actions I'm initiating now:
- Dylan/SRE: please triage Route53/DNS latencies and upstream timeouts, confirm if this is a cloud DNS problem vs our runtime.
- I'll spin up a temporary routing policy to fail requests to an eu-west-1 fallback pool and enable stricter per-customer concurrency limits for BrightCart to reduce retry amplification.
- Marissa/Evelyn: can you prep a short customer message and credits authorization if this persists?

Please keep the channel tight — include any updated error-rate samples and any Route53/AWS advisories you receive.

Soojín Lee
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: containment-playbook-0709.md (text)]
From: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Lin <rachel@brightcart.com>, Route53 Support <route53-support@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Spike in 5xx/429 across checkout region (us-west-2)

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed elevated DNS resolution latencies (us-west-2 resolvers) starting ~08:30 PDT across multiple customer endpoints; spike in NXDOMAIN and TCP connect timeouts to our agent pool.
- Our serving clusters in us-west-2 are healthy at the host level, but the upstream DNS delays are causing connection timeouts and client retries stack up, resulting in request queueing and 429s from our throttling layer.
- Correlation: increased Route53 latency metrics (per-route) and partial failures reported on AWS status page for the region.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:40):
1) Traffic steering: enabled policy to route BrightCart traffic to eu-west-1 fallback pool for model-calls that don't require strict geo affinity.
2) Circuit breaker: lowered BrightCart max concurrent tokens to 30 and increased backoff on the client-facing side to throttle retries.
3) KV-cache warmers: pre-warmed cache for frequent prefixes to reduce cold-start token generation.

Next: collect client retry headers, continue monitoring Route53, coordinate with AWS support. Attaching a short snapshot from our edge logs.

[Attachment: incident-snapshot-20260707.log (text)]

—Dylan
From: Route53 Support <route53-support@amazon.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 02:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DNS latency — us-west-2 operational advisory

Hello team,

We are investigating an increased latency and elevated error rates for a subset of Route53 resolvers in us-west-2 between 08:15–11:30 PDT on 2026-07-07. A subset of customers may have experienced higher-than-normal DNS propagation and resolution times; our engineers deployed mitigations at 10:50 PDT and are monitoring.

Please note: we are still rolling an incremental fix and tracking customer-reported cases under ticket #AWS-R53-11466. We'll update when the roll is complete.

Regards,
Route53 Support
From: Rachel Lin <rachel@brightcart.com>

Thanks for the fast response and for routing traffic — we saw an immediate drop in 429s after 09:45 PDT when traffic was steered. Two quick notes:
- We still observe intermittent 429s for short bursts when local clients aggressively retry (we've tightened our client backoff), but overall errors are down from ~12% to ~1.5%.
- Can Redwood provide a formal exec-facing summary and confirm planned post-mortem + credits? Our finance and product teams will expect a short write-up.

Appreciate the support,
Rachel
